builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Evaluating More with Less: Black-Box Test Selection for AI Agents
summary: The method replaces full benchmark re-execution after each change to an agent's model, prompt, scaffold, or tools with black-box selection of a task subset, using Category Partition for Success Rate estimation and LLM-as-judge scoring for early failure detection. Cost is limited to computing task features and optional judge calls, with no agent execution or historical results needed; the concrete result is a roughly 4.8x cost reduction at 0.8 percentage point estimation error on one benchmark-agent pair. Failure modes: no single strategy serves both objectives, results vary across the ten benchmarks evaluated, and difficulty estimates from heuristics or a judge may misrank tasks for a given agent, biasing the performance estimate or missing failures.
rationale: Black-box test selection requires no model internals or training, runs on embeddings and metadata any small team can compute, and directly cuts the dominant cost of evaluating proprietary agent configurations, but the two objectives (estimation versus failure detection) need different strategies, so workload-specific validation is warranted.
technique: Black-box test selection for agent evaluation

claims.statement: The method replaces full benchmark re-execution after each change to an agent's model, prompt, scaffold, or tools with black-box selection of a task subset, using Category Partition for Success Rate estimation and LLM-as-judge scoring for early failure detection. Cost is limited to computing task features and optional judge calls, with no agent execution or historical results needed; the concrete result is a roughly 4.8x cost reduction at 0.8 percentage point estimation error on one benchmark-agent pair. Failure modes: no single strategy serves both objectives, results vary across the ten benchmarks evaluated, and difficulty estimates from heuristics or a judge may misrank tasks for a given agent, biasing the performance estimate or missing failures.

For GPT 5.2 Codex on SWE-bench Verified, Category Partition selection reduces evaluation from 500 tasks ($225) to 100 tasks ($47) with 0.8 percentage point Success Rate estimation error; LLM-as-judge selection finds failures in 53.0% of selected tasks versus 27.4% for random sampling.
